solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lack of footwear bearing right label

indicators.note: footwear bearing something carries it within, so the shoe holds the other pieces

parts.note: a shoe is an item of footwear
a tag is a label tied on

explanation.surface: A shop has no shoes left that carry the correct label.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortage is a lack or insufficiency of something needed.

clue.text: Work hard on an advertising jingle

parts.note: to slog is to work hard and doggedly

explanation.surface: Someone toils over writing a catchy jingle for an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a catchphrase used in advertising, often set to a jingle.

clue.text: They're superior, taking six balls at cricket ground

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end
Lord's is the famous cricket ground in London

explanation.surface: Superior players face an over at a famous cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: An OVER is six deliveries in cricket; LORD'S, in north London, is the sport's best-known ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlords are rulers set above others, hence superior in rank.

clue.text: Total has to correspond

definitions.meaning: accounts that ... agree or match up

explanation.surface: A sum is said to need to match up with something.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is a reckoned count; as a verb it means to agree with another figure.

clue.text: How girls, after midnight, make spectacles of themselves?

indicators.note: after places the girls' word following the midnight letter

parts.note: the middle of the word night is its letter G
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: A question about how young women make fools of themselves late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midnight' is read as the middle of 'night', its central letter G; 'make spectacles of themselves' also hides the definition inside an idiom for behaving foolishly.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles and glasses are synonyms for eyewear.

clue.text: They are trained to fight dogs

definitions.meaning: fighters in the ring are trained pugilists
the boxer is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: Animals said to be trained for dogfights.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers are pugilists trained for the ring, and also a German breed of dog.

clue.text: Attack thus with a long formation

indicators.note: a formation is an arrangement, so these letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Troops attack in this manner, drawn up in an extended line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formation' rearranges THUS and A LONG together.
explanation.definitionFit: An onslaught is a fierce, sudden assault.

clue.text: No head on the beer? That is strange

indicators.note: no head means the opening letter of the drink is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
i.e. is the abbreviation for that is (id est)

explanation.surface: A drinker finds a flat pint with no froth odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No head on' removes the B of BEER, leaving EER.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means weird or uncanny, a sense of strangeness.

clue.text: An unexpected pleasure?

parts.note: the phrase describes a nice thing one did not see coming

explanation.surface: A happy event that arrives without warning.
explanation.definitionFit: A surprise is something unforeseen, often a pleasing one like a gift or party.

clue.text: Applied for leave on the next page

indicators.note: applied in the sense of worked or put to use, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A form for requesting time off continues on the following page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Applied' reads as requested, but it signals rearranging FOR LEAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Overleaf means on the other side of the sheet, the following page.

clue.text: One who takes great interest in business

definitions.text: One who takes great interest in business

parts.words: One who takes great interest in business
parts.note: interest is the money charged on a loan, and a great deal of it is exorbitant

explanation.surface: Someone keenly engaged in commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interest' seems to mean enthusiasm, but it is the charge on lent money.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurer lends money at extortionate rates of interest.

clue.text: Some passer-by from Belgrade?

indicators.note: some of means only part of the hyphenated word's letters are taken

explanation.surface: A pedestrian who happens to come from Belgrade.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgrade is the capital of Serbia, so a native there is a Serbian national.

clue.text: Put down a pound stake

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra
a lay is a bet or wager, as in to lay a stake

explanation.surface: Someone places a one-pound bet.
explanation.definitionFit: To allay fears is to quell or suppress them, as a revolt is put down.

clue.text: Woman had a rip in her dress and sobbed

parts.note: she is a pronoun for a woman
'd is the short form of had, as in she'd
a tear is a rip in fabric

explanation.surface: A woman cried because her dress was torn.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as she'd a tear, the wordplay says she had a rip; run together it is the phrase for weeping.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed tears is to cry, so the phrase means wept or sobbed.

clue.text: Directions taken by clergymen

explanation.surface: Instructions accepted by priests.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means commands, and holy orders are what a priest takes on being ordained.

clue.text: Sufficient for a joint operation in space?

definitions.text: Sufficient for a joint operation in space?

parts.words: Sufficient for a joint operation in space?
parts.note: a joint here is the arm's middle joint, and room for it to work is enough space

explanation.surface: Reads like a question about a joint space mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint operation' suggests a combined mission and 'space' outer space; really it is room to move one's arm joint.
explanation.definitionFit: Elbow room is enough space to move or act freely.

clue.text: They have no choice, poor chaps

definitions.meaning: from the proverb that the needy cannot be choosers
destitute people who ask for alms

explanation.surface: Unfortunate men left without options.
explanation.definitionFit: Beggars are the destitute, and the proverb says beggars can't be choosers.

clue.text: In control of a race taking two men over fifty miles

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

indicators.note: two signals the pronoun for a man is used twice

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A race won by two riders over a fifty-mile course.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at the helm is steering the ship, hence in charge.

clue.text: Marshal in Orange Order is admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let inside, so the short word goes within the rearranged letters
to order letters is to rearrange them into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A marshal is admitted into the Orange Order.
explanation.walkthrough: The Orange Order is a Protestant fraternal body from Northern Ireland; here 'Order' is a command to rearrange, not the organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: To marshal people or facts is to arrange and organise them.

clue.text: Lies with rib broken? Ridiculous

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a claim of lying there with a fractured rib.
explanation.definitionFit: Risible means laughable, so absurd enough to provoke ridicule.

clue.text: Tender raised for London statue

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards, so the word is turned around

parts.note: sore means tender or painful

explanation.surface: A bid is put in for a statue in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns SORE upwards. The statue known as Eros stands in Piccadilly Circus, London.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged figure atop the Shaftesbury Memorial in Piccadilly Circus is popularly called Eros.

clue.text: Go round with a list at half-term

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties taken in turn

indicators.note: half signals only the front two letters of the four-letter word are used

explanation.surface: Pupils take turns on a duty list during the school half-term holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes TE, the first half of 'term'; half-term is a short school holiday in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to turn or revolve, going round an axis.

clue.text: Put out trailer for the second test?

indicators.note: put out means disturbed or disarranged, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A film trailer released ahead of a sequel or second screening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' rearranges TRAILER; the 'test' is a case tried again in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A retrial is a case heard a second time, a second trial of the evidence.

clue.text: Rods we developed for the diviner

indicators.note: developed means worked into a new form, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Rods were made for the water diviner's use.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowser searches for underground water with a rod, a so-called water diviner.

clue.text: Missile base and plant

parts.note: an arrow is a missile shot from a bow
a root is a base or foundation

explanation.surface: A list of weapons, a launch site and a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrowroot is a tropical plant whose tubers yield a starch used in cooking.

clue.text: Cook using the right oven

parts.note: an oast is a kiln or oven for drying hops

explanation.surface: Instructions to cook using the proper oven.
explanation.walkthrough: An OAST is a kiln for drying hops, typical of Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast is to cook food with dry heat.

clue.text: Communist firm about belief

indicators.note: about means around, so the company letters surround the political word

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a red is a communist

explanation.surface: A communist company's attitude towards faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a creed, a set of beliefs one holds.

clue.text: Approach junction — it provides a long tail-back

parts.note: to come is to approach
a T is a T-junction, where one road meets another

explanation.surface: Near a road junction, causing a long queue of traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tail-back' suggests a traffic jam, but it means a tail streaming back behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet is a celestial body that trails a long glowing tail behind it.

clue.text: Lined up during altercation

parts.note: in means during, as in in the night
a row is an altercation, a heated argument

explanation.surface: Arranged in line while a quarrel goes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Things in a row are set out one after another in a line.

clue.text: Business head shows resolution

parts.note: a firm is a business
a ness is a headland or promontory, as in Sheerness

explanation.surface: A company boss displays determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is a headland, a NESS in place names like Sheerness.
explanation.definitionFit: Firmness is steadfastness of purpose, resolve.

clue.text: Wrong note goes to doctor — so bury a patient?

indicators.note: wrong means disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: MB is the qualification Bachelor of Medicine, so a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor's mistaken prescription note ends in a patient's burial.
explanation.definitionFit: To entomb is to place in a tomb, that is, to bury.

clue.text: Veteran convict?

definitions.meaning: a convict serves time, so a long-serving one has done time before

explanation.surface: An experienced prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-timer is a veteran, and playfully one who has done time inside.
